title: Admissible free finite-group quotient of a separated scheme
statement: Let $M$ be a separated scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $G$ be a finite abstract group acting on $M$ by scheme automorphisms. Set $G_T=\coprod_{g\in G}T$ for each scheme $T$. Suppose that the action is free: $(g,m)\mapsto(gm,m)$ defines a monomorphism $G_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\times M\to M\times M$, meaning injectivity on sections over every test scheme. Suppose every point orbit of $G$ in $|M|$ lies in an affine open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. The fppf sheafification [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the orbit presheaf $T\mapsto M(T)/G_T(T)$ is represented by a separated scheme $Q$, where separated means that the absolute diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The map $q:M\to Q$ is finite etale and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], and the action map identifies $G_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\times M$ with $M\times_QM$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every scheme $T\to Q$, $M\times_QT\to T$ represents the fppf orbit quotient of the base-changed action. Every $G$-invariant map from $M$ to an fppf sheaf factors uniquely through $Q$. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $q$ identifies $Q(\Omega)$ with the set of $G$-orbits in $M(\Omega)$. If $M$ is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover), then $Q$ is quasi-compact. No Noetherianity, finite-type hypothesis on $M$, or invertibility of $|G|$ is required.

proof.text: Given an affine open U containing the point orbit of x, take the intersection W of a(g) inverse-image U over all g in G. Each translate is affine, and finite intersections of affine opens of a separated scheme are affine (Mathlib IsAffineOpen.iInf). Every orbit point lies in W. Reindexing the finite intersection by right multiplication proves a(g) inverse-image W = W. This proves the hypothesis of the invariant-affine presentation lemma without the general finite locally free groupoid shrinking theorem.

proof.text: The fold coproduct_G M to M is finite by the finite sigmaDesc instance. The pullback of q by itself is isomorphic to this fold through the specified kernel pair, hence finite. The etale surjection q is a singleton fppf and thus fpqc covering. Apply isFinite_of_fpqc_cover to this cover to descend finiteness to q.

proof.text: For any fppf sheaf F, apply its singleton-cover sheaf axiom to q. Yoneda identifies a transformation h_M to F with a section of F(M); the kernel-pair lift proves compatibility of its local sections. Existence and uniqueness of gluing give unique descent of every equalizing transformation. The presheaf coequalizer universal property now constructs eta and proves its required bijectivity for every F. No representable descent theorem or general FppfKernelPairQuotientDescent declaration is used.

proof.text: Construct the two base-changed relation maps by pullback.lift, with all four required projection equations. The pullback universal property proves that they form the kernel pair of the base-changed q. The latter is an fppf cover by stability of flatness, local finite presentation and surjectivity. Apply the singleton-cover descent and coequalizer argument from the preceding step. For groupwise invariant maps, use sheaf separatedness for the open cover of the relation by its G-summands to prove equality on the entire relation, including disconnected tests; then apply the same descent.

proof.text: A finite surjection lifts every algebraically closed field point by exists_comp_eq_of_isFinite_of_surjective. Equal images give a point of the kernel pair. Every map from Spec of a field into the coproduct factors through a single summand: its spectrum has one point, and that summand is an open immersion containing the entire image. The projection equations give y=a(g)x. Conversely compose the kernel-pair equality with the g-summand to show invariance of q.

lean.note: The canonical action relation is the coproduct of G copies of M, with fold source and componentwise action target. Its pointwise presheaf coequalizer is the orbit presheaf under locally constant G-valued labels, including disconnected tests. The universal property of sheafificationAdjunction specifies its fppf sheafification. IsPullback fixes the original action kernel pair; the base-changed action maps are determined by both pullback projections. Explicit universes u,v,w allow any finite abstract group and arbitrary larger set-valued sheaves.
